subject.title: [Feature] Re-enable dev channel distribution tag for npm releases

question: Should the supported development channel remain a GitHub-main checkout, or should OpenClaw operate a continuously published npm `dev` snapshot channel?
rationale: Both choices are viable product contracts, but the npm route changes release security, package identity, operator workflow, and support expectations; source inspection cannot safely select that policy alone.

options.title: Keep dev Git-only
options.body: Formally document `openclaw update --channel dev` and the main-checkout installer as the supported development path, and retire npm-dev references.

options.title: Sponsor npm snapshots
options.body: Design a dedicated, trusted snapshot-release workflow with immutable versioning, provenance, registry checks, rollback rules, and focused release tests before enabling `@dev`.

recommendation.title: Keep dev Git-only
recommendation.body: Formally document `openclaw update --channel dev` and the main-checkout installer as the supported development path, and retire npm-dev references.

likelyOwner.reason: Current release workflow and development-channel history, plus the existing issue analysis, point to this release area.
